griefTypes.description: Loss is not a monolithic event but a multifaceted experience that varies based on the nature of the relationship, the circumstances of the event, and the societal recognition of the grief

types.name: Normal (Uncomplicated) Grief
types.description: The expected and standard response to the loss of a close attachment. Involves emotional (sadness, anger), physical (insomnia, appetite changes), and cognitive (confusion, preoccupation) reactions that generally attenuate as the individual finds integrated grief.

types.name: Anticipatory Grief
types.description: Grief that occurs prior to a loss, typically after a terminal diagnosis or significant decline in health. A proactive process of preparing for the inevitable, characterized by higher levels of fear and anxiety.

types.name: Complicated Grief
types.description: When the natural movement from acute grief to integrated grief is derailed. Affects approximately 7% of bereaved people. Characterized by excessive rumination, avoidance of reminders, and persistent intense yearning.

types.name: Prolonged Grief Disorder
types.description: Formalized clinical diagnosis (WHO/APA) for grief that remains disabling and pervasive beyond 6 to 12 months.

types.name: Persistent Complex Bereavement Disorder
types.description: DSM-5 diagnostic term, precursor to Prolonged Grief Disorder.

types.name: Disenfranchised Grief
types.description: Grief experienced when a loss cannot be openly acknowledged, socially validated, or publicly mourned. Examples: death of ex-spouse, secret lover, pet.

types.name: Ambiguous Loss Type I
types.description: Physical Absence/Psychological Presence - 'gone but not for sure'. Loved one is physically missing (kidnapping, war, disaster) but remains psychologically present because there is no proof of death.

types.name: Ambiguous Loss Type II
types.description: Psychological Absence/Physical Presence - 'here but not here'. Person is physically present but psychologically gone due to dementia, Alzheimer's, brain injury, or severe addiction.

types.name: Collective Grief
types.description: Shared experience of bereavement felt by a group, community, or nation after a catastrophic event (terrorist attack, school shooting, pandemic).

types.name: Ecological Grief
types.description: Grief felt in response to ecological degradation or loss of landscapes, species, ecosystems. Sub-forms: transitional loss, lifeworld loss, shattered future dreams.

types.name: Historical Trauma/Grief
types.description: Cumulative emotional and psychological wounding over lifespan and across generations from massive group trauma (Holocaust, slavery, internment).

types.name: Intergenerational Trauma
types.description: Transmission of unresolved grief and psychological symptoms from one generation to the next within a family system.

types.name: Vicarious Grief
types.description: Empathetic grief experienced by professionals (healthcare workers, first responders) who witness trauma and losses of others.

types.name: Traumatic Grief
types.description: Complex mixture of trauma and loss when death is sudden, violent, or preventable. Often requires simultaneous PTSD and bereavement treatment.

types.name: Cumulative Grief (Bereavement Overload)
types.description: Multiple losses occurring in close proximity - cannot process one before another arrives. Results in emotional exhaustion.

types.name: Secondary Loss
types.description: Peripheral losses following a primary loss: financial security, social role, identity, routines, future plans.

types.name: Inhibited Grief
types.description: Mourning where individual suppresses reaction to maintain professional facade or protect others. Often leads to physical manifestations (headaches, digestive issues).

types.name: Delayed Grief
types.description: Reaction postponed for weeks, months, or years. Often emerges suddenly after a separate minor event makes the original loss 'real'.

types.name: Absent Grief
types.description: Few or no outward signs of grieving. May be due to total denial or psychological freezing of grief process.

types.name: Masked Grief
types.description: Symptoms like impulsive behavior or physical illness without recognizing they are related to a loss.

types.name: Exaggerated Grief
types.description: Extreme reaction where symptoms intensify over time rather than waning. May lead to self-destructive behaviors or clinical psychosis.

types.name: Abbreviated Grief
types.description: Short-lived but genuine grief response. Sometimes seen when deceased is quickly 'replaced' or if significant mourning was completed anticipatorily.

types.name: Distorted (Conflicted) Grief
types.description: Atypical reactions involving intense self-blame, hostility, or odd behavioral changes.

types.name: Chronic Grief
types.description: Prolongation of intense symptoms appropriate in acute phase but persisting for years without resolution.

types.name: Dissonant Grief
types.description: Clash between individual's natural grieving style and societal/cultural expectations they feel they must meet.

types.name: Intuitive Grief
types.description: Affective style - processing loss through deep waves of emotion, crying, sharing feelings with community.

types.name: Instrumental Grief
types.description: Cognitive style - processing loss through problem-solving, activity, internal reflection. Often expresses anger more readily than sadness.

types.name: Blended Grief
types.description: Most common style - fluid movement between cognitive/physical processing and emotional expression.

types.name: Complicated Spiritual Grief
types.description: Spiritual struggle where loss leads to crisis of faith, feeling abandoned or punished by God, estranged from religious community.

types.name: Non-finite Loss
types.description: Continuous loss lacking clear conclusion. Discrepancy between actual life and life one 'should have had'. Common in chronic illness, infertility.

types.name: Living Loss
types.description: Ongoing grief tied to life-altering events where person is still alive (child with chronic disability, partner with degenerative illness).

types.name: Chronic Sorrow
types.description: Periodic, lifelong sadness that re-emerges at developmental milestones in response to living losses or non-finite losses.

types.name: Grief for Self
types.description: Bereavement for loss of personal events, financial security, milestones, career, identity.

types.name: Moral Injury
types.description: Psychological and spiritual burden from actions/inactions that violate core moral beliefs. Results in profound shame and loss of trust.

types.name: Silent Grief
types.description: Masked grief where individual hides pain behind facade of false happiness to avoid burdening others.

types.name: Compounded Grief
types.description: Grief intensified by multiple simultaneous or cascading losses - sense of 'losing everything'.

types.name: Indefinite Loss
types.description: For carers of cancer patients - constant heightened awareness of mortality and inability to plan for future.

types.name: Doubt-Related Struggle
types.description: Cognitive spiritual grief - troubled by questions about religion or spirituality that previously felt certain.

types.name: Struggle of Ultimate Meaning
types.description: Existential grief - concern that life may not matter or that one's existence makes no difference.

types.name: Desecration
types.description: Specialized sacred loss - perceiving a manifestation of God or sacred bond as violated or defiled.
